I will still plant all 10.1 mu with cotton. I have done cotton many years, so I will not make big changes unless I see a clear gain. On my land, the safest way is to start from what usually works, then push a little where yield can drop if fertilizer is short. Cotton eats fertilizer in stages, so I will put most of the phosphorus and part of the nitrogen and potassium in the ground before or at planting, then I will topdress the rest around square formation and early boll setting. I have well water, so I will use that advantage and not let the field stay dry in the key time. My farm is not tiny but not very big either, so I can still manage it with family labor and maybe a little hired help if work piles up. I watch cost closely, but I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and one extra spray than lose bolls and regret it later. Around here, if cotton looks weak in July, yield falls fast, so I will keep fertilizer, water, and pest control a little on the safe side.
